status_reason: Evolves standalone ML learning algorithms with no agent harness and no self-modification loop; authors drop self-reflexivity.

paper.title: AutoML-Zero: Evolving Machine Learning Algorithms From Scratch
paper.central_claim: Complete machine learning algorithms can be discovered from scratch by evolutionary search over programs built from basic mathematical operations, rediscovering backpropagation-trained networks and, with further search, algorithms that outperform a hand-designed 2-layer network and adapt to task types.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to the worker; null by design (no probing).

rationale: Out of scope: evolutionary AutoML search for learner programs (architecture+optimiser) with self-reflexivity explicitly dropped; no harness component or self-modifying loop. Not scored; nearest card H14 needs scope revision if wanted.

evidence.quote: it is possible today to automatically discover complete machine learning algorithms just using basic mathematical operations as building blocks
evidence.support_explanation: Object evolved: complete ML algorithms (model structure + initialisation + learning rule) as programs.

evidence.quote: We share similar goals in searching for learning algorithms, but focus on common machine learning tasks and have dropped the self-reflexivity requirement.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors explicitly drop self-improvement/self-reflexivity: the search improves a separate learner, not the searching system.

evidence.quote: We represent algorithms as computer programs that act on a small virtual memory with separate address spaces for scalar, vector and matrix variables
evidence.support_explanation: Retained artifact is a Setup/Predict/Learn program for supervised classification/regression, not an agent harness component.

evidence.quote: This parent is then copied and mutated to produce a child algorithm that is added to the population, while the oldest algorithm in the population is removed.
evidence.support_explanation: Regularised evolution with random mutation; no LLM or reflective critique; feedback is task accuracy.

evidence.quote: The candidate algorithms perform better in 13 out of 20 experiments.
evidence.support_explanation: Selection result on held-out class pairs against a 2-layer net.

evidence.quote: we treat all the constants in the best evolved algorithm as hyperparameters and tune them jointly through RS using the validation set
evidence.support_explanation: Human-pipeline step required before final evaluation; plus manual decoupling in Sec.5.

evidence.quote: the algorithm evolves the exact prediction function used by the teacher and hard-codes its weights
evidence.support_explanation: Single-task evolution can hard-code weights, showing the object can contain weights for D=1.

evidence.quote: holding out the CIFAR-10 test set for the final evaluation
evidence.support_explanation: Clean selection/test separation in the evaluation protocol (for the model-algorithm claim).

signatures.object: Learning algorithm programs (Setup/Predict/Learn over a 65-op vocabulary): model structure, initialisation and optimiser rule
signatures.information: Task accuracy on projected binary CIFAR-10/MNIST proxy tasks; no gradients or neural-network assumptions
signatures.operation: Regularised evolution: tournament selection, mutation (insert/remove, randomise, modify argument), functional-equivalence caching, hurdles, migration
signatures.output: Best evolved algorithm compared with 2-layer neural net and logistic regression on CIFAR-10 test
signatures.conditions: Search on proxy tasks, final tuning of constants by random search, manual decoupling of coupled hyperparameters
signatures.selection_rule/data: T_search / T_select (36/9 class pairs), CIFAR-10 test held out
signatures.persistence: Population of programs; final selected program
signatures.claimed_effect: Evolved algorithm 84.06 +/- 0.10% vs 82.22 +/- 0.17% (2-layer NN) on binary CIFAR-10
signatures.failure_boundary: Search space lacks conv/batchnorm; human tuning/decoupling needed

gap.author_gap: AutoML search spaces rely on expert-designed building blocks and carefully composed constraints, biasing results toward human-designed algorithms.
gap.checked_gap: Not evaluated against the harness-RSI question: the gap concerns AutoML search-space design, not whether a deployed system improves its own non-weight components from its own execution feedback.
gap.lineage/closest_adjacent: NAS and hyperparameter search; learned optimizers; genetic programming of learning rules (Bengio 1994, Bello 2017); program synthesis; self-improving programs (Schmidhuber 1987) which the authors cite and set aside.
gap.method_response: Instruction-level program search with regularised evolution.
gap.unresolved: Not pursued because the paper is out of scope.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: Names the tacit assumption that AutoML needs expert-designed layers and rules of backpropagation, relaxes it by searching over basic operations, and shows rediscovery of backprop-trained nets. No theory.
matches.success_failure_checks: RE-4 (differentiation from similar prior moves such as Bengio 1994, Bello 2017) partially met.
matches.reason: Recorded for coverage only; scope decision (out_of_scope) does not depend on pattern matching.

rs_pattern.reason: Pattern recorded provisionally; paper is out of harness-RSI scope.
rs_pattern.resolves_problem_reason: Not evaluated for the harness-RSI problem.

unassigned: Non-LLM evolutionary search over ML-algorithm programs. Nearest card population_search_executable_fitness/H14 is defined for LLM mutation of agent-relevant programs; the retained object here is a learning algorithm (model structure plus optimiser), i.e. the model/training layer.
revision_proposals: If the project wants classical program evolution / AutoML covered, add an explicit scope and card revision (A3); not decided in batch.

claims.text: Evolution discovers neural networks trained by backprop from scratch and algorithms that beat a 2-layer net on binary CIFAR-10.
claims.setting: Projected proxy tasks; CIFAR-10 test held out
claims.allowed_conclusion: Not assessed for harness-level RSI (out of scope).

assessment.unresolved: Scope decision only; no quality scoring.

scope_decision.basis: The evolutionary search improves a standalone supervised learning algorithm (model structure, initialisation and optimiser) on classification tasks. No agent or deployed system runs tasks and modifies its own prompt/skill/tool/workflow/memory/evaluator/agent code from its own execution feedback; authors state they dropped the self-reflexivity requirement (E002). The retained artifact is the model/training layer, not a harness component (EVIDENCE.md scope; A3 judged by evaluated object).
scope_decision.sensitivity_note: Alternative reading as a B-type program-evolution component (nearest card H14) is possible if scope is widened to non-LLM program evolution; that needs an explicit domain-card revision rather than a low score (A3). Without a scope change this record carries no score.
